sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Governance establishes who owns the agent, what it is allowed to do and how its behavior is reviewed.

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

sections.title: 52.1 Agent inventory
sections.body:
Every production agent should have an inventory record.

```json
{
  "agent_id": "procurement_reviewer",
  "version": "3.2",
  "business_owner": "procurement",
  "technical_owner": "ai_platform",
  "risk_tier": "high",
  "allowed_capabilities": [
    "supplier.read",
    "budget.read",
    "proposal.create"
  ],
  "prohibited_capabilities": [
    "payment.execute"
  ],
  "approval_policy": "procurement-v4",
  "max_delegation_depth": 2,
  "status": "active"
}
```

sections.title: 52.3 Kill switches
sections.body:
An emergency stop should allow authorized operators to disable a particular capability, agent version, tenant workload or entire execution category.

The policy must be enforced at the tool gateway and authoritative service boundaries.

Updating a system prompt with "stop executing" is not an operational kill switch.

Already completed external operations must be reconciled separately.
